review: Reviewer agrees: जुग = युग / the age, as a unit in the list of units of time.
Reviewer agrees: अति उकुति = अत्युक्ति, hyperbole (the tears filling the ocean is plainly an exaggeration).

Reviewer agrees with the writer: कहेसि (3rd sg. past) with तेहि = her and सो = he in the next half; Rāvaṇa reassures Mandodarī and returns to the council. Mandodarī's realisation in line 1 also fits only this reading.

issue: नाना बिधि तेहि कहेसि बुझाई: who consoles whom. कहेसि is a third-person singular past; the context is Rāvaṇa reassuring Mandodarī before going to court.
our reading: Rāvaṇa reassured her (तेहि = her) in many ways, then went to the council.
alternatives: Mandodarī explained to him in many ways (Gita Press Hindi), but he went back to the council regardless.

issue: जुग in the list of time units: yuga (age) or "pair".
our reading: युग / the age, as one of the units of time.
alternatives: जुग = two, read with the neighbouring words; unlikely in a list of units.

issue: अति उकुति: "hyperbole" (अत्युक्ति) or simply "very (apt) saying".
our reading: अतिशयोक्ति / hyperbole.
alternatives: a very fine (witty) saying of Hanumān.

review: Reviewer agrees: महान् = Viṣṇu (the Great One) fits the list of deities (Śiva, Brahmā, the moon) and is the usual reading; the mahat alternative is rightly recorded.
Reviewer agrees: करहु is 2nd person addressed to Rāma right after अंगद उठेउ, and so17ख (अस बिचारि) is Aṅgada's own thought; Aṅgada speaking line 2 is the natural reading.
Reviewer agrees: 10.cau2 ends चला भवन कहि बचन कठोरा, and तोहि with the medicine simile is those harsh parting words.

issue: महान in 'चित्त महान': Viṣṇu (the Great One) or the mahat principle (cosmic intellect).
our reading: महान् (विष्णु) / the Great One (Viṣṇu) is his citta.
alternatives: Mahat, the great principle of Sāṃkhya, is his citta.

issue: Who speaks line 2 (करहु, addressed to Rāma): Aṅgada on rising, or the poet's aside.
our reading: Aṅgada rises and says it to Śrī Rāma.
alternatives: Tulasīdāsa's own remark addressed to Rāma.

issue: Line 1 (तोहि): Prahasta's parting words to Rāvaṇa (the कठोर बचन of 10.cau2), or the narrator's comment.
our reading: Prahasta's parting words, addressed to his father.
alternatives: The narrator's comment on Rāvaṇa.

review: Agree with the doubt: the subject of पठावा is unstated; the impersonal rendering is the safe plain reading (Aṅgada sending a demon is less likely than the gate demons doing so). Owner to decide.

issue: तुरत निसाचर एक पठावा names no subject: Aṅgada may have sent a demon to announce himself, or the demons at the gate sent one of their own to Rāvaṇa.
our reading: Left impersonal: a demon was sent at once and gave Rāvaṇa the news.
alternatives: Aṅgada sent a demon to tell Rāvaṇa of his arrival (Gita Press).

issue: सुनु सब कीसा: सब with ते (they are not all heroes) or with कीसा (listen, all you monkeys / monkey)
our reading: they are not all heroes; listen, monkey (Rāvaṇa addresses Aṅgada alone)
alternatives: birds cross the ocean, yet they are not heroes; listen, all you monkeys

issue: सीता मैं हारी: Aṅgada stakes Sītā as a wager
our reading: Śrī Rāma will turn back and I have lost Sītā (as a wager)
alternatives: I shall have lost (the cause of) Sītā; I give up claim to Sītā

review: Agree: नीचा as 'that lowly one' (Mārīca) is the plain reading; Mandodarī would not call Rāvaṇa नीच; alternatives fairly recorded.
Agree: 'bring it to an end' for पूर देहु fits the next line (worship Rāma); alternatives fairly recorded.
Agree: आतुर as an adjective of नारी is the plain reading; 'the sick' is a fair alternative.

issue: नीचा: who is 'low' — Mārīca, or Rāvaṇa addressed, or 'taking him to be low'
our reading: that lowly one (Mārīca): you did not heed even his word
alternatives: the lowly Mārīca knew the arrow's power
you did not heed him, thinking him low
you, base one, did not heed him

issue: अजहुँ पूर पिय देहु: sense of पूर देना
our reading: even now bring it (the enmity) to an end
alternatives: make good the loss / make amends even now
complete (fill up) what is lacking

issue: आतुर: adjective of नारी (distressed women) or a separate group (the sick)
our reading: children and frightened women weep
alternatives: children, the sick and women weep

issue: बिसमय: wonder or dismay (विषाद)?
our reading: wonder (विस्मय): the gods watch now in wonder, now in delight
alternatives: dismay/grief (खेद), as when the monkeys suffer

issue: Who is अकुलान, the she-crocodile or Hanumān?
our reading: the she-crocodile, in a frenzy, seized his foot
alternatives: then Hanumān was troubled (when seized)

issue: सब बिधि सुखद परम हित जानी: whom did Sumitrā know as giving joy and the greatest well-wisher?
our reading: Rāma: knowing me (Rāma) a source of joy in every way and your truest well-wisher
alternatives: Lakṣmaṇa: knowing you would give me every comfort and be my greatest good

issue: सहोदर literally 'of the same womb', though Lakṣmaṇa is Sumitrā's son
our reading: a brother of one's own blood
alternatives: full brother, born of the same mother (literal)

review: Agree with the doubt: the plain reading of the words is epithets, but Gita Press reads Devāntaka and Narāntaka; the owner should decide. The Hindi list leaves open whether the epithets qualify Durmukha, which the doubt already covers.
Agree with the doubt; the address reading (हे स्वामी / My lord) is the usual one and fits Kumbhakarṇa speaking to his king.
Agree with the doubt; the address to Vibhīṣaṇa reads naturally, the alternative is possible.
Agree with the doubt and with our reading (Kumbhakarṇa took him for dead, so Sugrīva slipped free).

issue: सुररिपु and मनुज अहारी: plain epithets ("foe of the gods", "eater of men") or the names Devāntaka and Narāntaka (Rāvaṇa's sons, slain earlier in the Vālmīki account)
our reading: plain epithets, as separate warriors
alternatives: Devāntaka and Narāntaka by name
epithets of Durmukha

issue: प्रभु: Kumbhakarṇa addressing Rāvaṇa ("my lord") or qualifying the god (that Lord, the god)
our reading: address to Rāvaṇa (हे स्वामी / My lord)
alternatives: you made enmity with that Lord, the god whose servants are Śiva, Brahmā and the gods

issue: बीर: address to Vibhīṣaṇa or qualifying Kumbhakarṇa himself (मैं कालबस बीर)
our reading: address to Vibhīṣaṇa (हे वीर / brave one)
alternatives: I, a warrior, have fallen under death

issue: निबुकि गयउ तेहि मृतक प्रतीती: Kumbhakarṇa believed Sugrīva dead, or Sugrīva slipped away like a dead thing
our reading: Sugrīva slipped free because Kumbhakarṇa believed him dead
alternatives: Sugrīva, as if dead, slid out of his armpit

issue: अरुन: whether 'red' goes with the lotus eyes (राजीव लोचन अरुन) or with the body reddened by drops of blood (अरुन तन सोनित कनी).
our reading: the lotus eyes are red; drops of blood are on the body
alternatives: lotus eyes; the body red with drops of blood

issue: बोले अंगदादि कपि नाना: बोले as 'spoke to' or 'called, summoned' (Awadhi बोलना = to call).
our reading: spoke to Aṅgada and many other monkeys
alternatives: summoned Aṅgada and many other monkeys

issue: सेन समेत रहेहु तीनिउ जन: stay with Lakṣmaṇa along with the army, or stay (here) with the army.
our reading: you three stay with the army
alternatives: you three go with him (Lakṣmaṇa) along with the army
you three stay behind here with the army

issue: जय अनंत: Ananta may be Lakṣmaṇa (Śeṣa, slayer of Meghanāda; cf. lanka.75.do75, 76.cau4) or Śrī Rāma, whose glory the gods are singing.
our reading: kept as Ananta, unidentified
alternatives: Lakṣmaṇa as Ananta
Śrī Rāma, the infinite

review: Agree with the writer: खर = donkeys (a recognised ill omen beside jackals and vultures); keep the reading.
Agree: नाना बान = of many colours (बाना/वर्ण); 'with many arrows' does not fit winged mountains. Hindi rendering fixed separately.

issue: नाना बान: of many colours (बाना/वर्ण) or with many arrows?
our reading: of many hues: flocks of winged mountains of many colours
alternatives: (flying) with many arrows

issue: कराल खर रव: खर as donkeys, or as an adjective (harsh) of the cries?
our reading: donkeys, with harsh and fearful cries
alternatives: jackals and vultures raising terrible, harsh cries (no donkeys)

review: Agree it is a genuine doubt: in this chhanda's Prakrit-style doubling (कटक्कट, बोल्लहिं) खग्ग may be खड्ग 'sword', but it may equally be खग 'bird' doubled (the usual reading). Keep the doubt for the owner.
Agree it is a genuine doubt: कंपति can be कं+पति 'lord of waters' (the ocean, fitting the list कमठ भू भूधर) as well as a doubled 'trembles'; our glossary has 'trembles'. Keep for the owner.

issue: खग्ग: sword (Prakrit of खड्ग) or birds (खग) entangled among the skulls
our reading: warriors grapple, tangled among skulls and swords
alternatives: birds, entangled in the skulls, fight one another

issue: मंदोदरी उर कंप कंपति: कंपति read as 'trembles' (doubling the verb) or as a noun for the ocean (in the list of things that feared)
our reading: Mandodarī's heart shook and trembled; the Tortoise, earth and mountains feared
alternatives: the ocean, the Tortoise, the earth and the mountains feared

review: agree: the single अस कहि after सठहु … covers both half-lines, so 'spoken' is the plain reading; the doubt is rightly recorded
agree: घाल as a makeweight/trifle (Platts) fits 'नहिं गनै' best; doubt rightly recorded

issue: भयउँ एक मैं इन्ह के लेखें: whether Rāvaṇa says this aloud or only thinks it; the verse has a single अस कहि after the following half-line.
our reading: spoken: Rāvaṇa said: So by their reckoning I am only one now!
alternatives: thought to himself (Gita Press: रावणने सोचा), with only सठहु … spoken

issue: घालि नहिं ता कहुँ गनै: घालि read as घाल (a makeweight, a trifle), not 'placing'.
our reading: does not count him as worth the least trifle
alternatives: does not count him at all (घालि as an intensive 'cast aside')

issue: नयसीला: qualifies Hanumān (मारुति) alone, or all those named
our reading: Hanumān, wise in counsel
alternatives: all of you, skilled in right counsel

issue: कहा न माना: whose words were not heeded (Mandodarī's own, or anyone's counsel)
our reading: you would not heed what you were told (anyone's counsel)
alternatives: you did not heed my words

issue: चरन रति अति निर्मली: Sītā's pure love for the feet of the Lord of Kosala, or an epithet of the Lord's feet
our reading: Sītā hails the Lord of Kosala, whose feet (adored by Śiva) she loves with a wholly pure love
alternatives: the Lord of Kosala, whose feet are adored by Śiva and loved with pure devotion (by all devotees)

issue: दूषन हा: slayer of the demon Dūṣaṇa, or destroyer of faults (दूषण = fault)
our reading: slayer of Dūṣaṇa
alternatives: destroyer of faults
both senses at once

issue: प्रथम प्रेम अनुमाना: Rāma considered Daśaratha's former love (from his earthly life), or Rāma first weighed his love
our reading: mindful of his father's love of old
alternatives: first perceiving his father's love, Rāma looked at him and gave him firm knowledge

review: Agree: दर as fear (Skt. dara) fits बारय; the 'conch' reading is strained. Keep our reading.
Agree: बीर = brother (Bharata), picked up by अनुज in the next line. Keep our reading.
Agree it is open (जिनस = kinds/sorts, also goods, attire); our neutral 'in such variety' covers both. Keep.
Agree: सहित reads most plainly as 'together with the monkeys he gave'. Keep our reading.

issue: उदार पार मन and परमं दर: 'generous and beyond the mind' or 'generous one who carries the mind across'; दर as fear (भय) rather than conch.
our reading: you are generous and beyond the reach of the mind; drive away my great fear
alternatives: generous one who takes the mind across
you are a conch to the Mandara churning the ocean (दर = conch)

issue: बीर: object 'brother' (Bharata, Awadhi बीर = brother) or an address to Vibhīṣaṇa 'O hero'.
our reading: I shall not find my brother alive
alternatives: O hero, I shall not find him alive

issue: नाना जिनस देखि सब कीसा: the monkeys of many kinds, or the monkeys decked in many kinds of things.
our reading: seeing all the monkeys in such variety
alternatives: seeing the monkeys in their many kinds of attire
seeing monkeys of many breeds

issue: कपिन्ह सहित बिप्रन्ह कहुँ दान: the Lord with the monkeys gave gifts to the Brahmins, or gave gifts to the Brahmins and to the monkeys.
our reading: together with the monkeys he gave gifts to the Brahmins
alternatives: he gave gifts to the Brahmins and the monkeys

review: Agree with the doubt: मन करि देखु बिचार can be 'reflect in the mind' or an address 'O mind'; the plain reading kept is fine for the owner to decide
Agree with the doubt: नाव नाव कहँ may be the cry 'boat, where is the boat' or 'called people for boats'; our reading is the natural one

issue: मन करि देखु बिचार: मन as the place of reflection or as an address to the mind
our reading: reflect in your mind and see
alternatives: O mind, reflect and see (address to the mind)

issue: नाव नाव कहँ: what Guha cries out
our reading: A boat! Where is a boat?
alternatives: called people for boats, crying 'boat, boat'
